note: Source-precedence tier 1 targets: the 11 manufacturers behind the 139 matched active sauna SKUs. Build Brief v2 said '~15 manufacturers'; the catalogue says 11. Reported rather than rounded to the brief.
why_every_product_url_template_is_null: STILL ALL NULL AFTER DISCOVER RUN 3 (2026-09-15), and that run is why.

Discover run 3 succeeded across all 11 vendors in 1m38s. It reported robots.txt status and homepage reachability -- and NOTHING about product URLs, because as written it requested only /robots.txt and /. robots.txt and a homepage do not contain a URL pattern, so the run produced no evidence any template could be filled from. Filling one anyway would have been writing from memory, which is the failure this list exists to prevent.
TWO DEEPER PROBLEMS the run exposed, both of which must be settled before a template means anything:

(1) product_url_template is substituted as .format(handle=handle), where handle is OUR InHouse Wellness Shopify handle -- 'arosa-4p-barrel-sauna', '1-2-person-infrared-sauna-hemlock-chromotherapy', 'hand-finished-precut-sauna-kit'. Those are our store's marketing slugs and cannot appear in a manufacturer's URL space. Even a correct path shape would request pages that do not exist.

(2) Every vendor row here declares model_key ('sku' for 9 of 11, 'title' for Medical Saunas) and scripts/fetch_manufacturer_specs.py never reads it. The registry states the right idea and the fetcher ignores it.

WHAT DISCOVER NOW COLLECTS, so the next run can settle it: Sitemap: directives already present in the robots.txt we fetch (free), those sitemaps with one level of sitemap-index following and a robots check before each request, product-looking links from the homepage body we already had, and -- the decisive test -- whether any REAL product URL of theirs contains one of OUR SKUs. product_urls_seen > 0 with sku_matches empty means their URLs are keyed on something we do not hold, and no format string will reach them. That is a finding, not a licence to guess.

A guessed template does not fail safely. inh-seo/CLAUDE.md records a followed redirect answering from /collections/best-infrared-saunas while the requested URL was a product page, putting a category page's FAQ into a report as a product specification. The fetch succeeded and the content was real; the ATTRIBUTION was wrong. tests/test_manufacturer_discovery.py asserts that /collections/... is never accepted as a product path, and that no template may be set for a vendor without sample_product_urls AND sku_matches in the discovery file.
Meanwhile the fetcher SKIPS any vendor whose template is null and records NEEDS_URL_TEMPLATE. That is the correct behaviour, not a gap.
